simple.meaning: כֶּסֶא (keçeʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, fulness or the full moon , i.e. its festival.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: כֶּסֶא (H3677) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 81:4, with occurrences in Psalms, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כֶּסֶא (H3677) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in כֶּסֶא (H3677) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: כֶּסֶא (keçeʼ) / H3677 is traced through Psalms 81:4, Proverbs 7:20 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, fulness or the full moon , i.e. its festival
definitions.full: H3677. kese or keseh כֶּ֫סֶא Prov 7:20 , כֶּ֫סֶה Psa 81:4 noun [masculine] full moon (compare Aramaic ; origin dubious, compare Lag Symn. i. 93 ; perhaps Assyrian loan-word; compare Assyrian kusêu , headdress or cap , = agû, id. , and also full moon (as tiara of moon-god ?), Dl HWB, sub kusêu, kubšu, agû ; yet see Brock) — הַכּ ׳לְיוֺם Prov 7:20 ; as a feast-day, ׳בַּכּ Psa 81:4 (opposed to בַּחֹדֶשׁ , at the new moon ).

occurrences.englishText: For it is a statute for Israel,
He has taken a bag of money with him.
